questions.question: Which of the following is the molecular mass of HNO₃?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**63 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The molecular mass of a compound is calculated by summing the atomic masses of its constituent elements.
 
• For HNO₃, the atomic masses are: H (1 u), N (14 u), and O (16 u).
 
• The total molecular mass is calculated as follows: 1u+14u+3×16u=63u" id="MathJax-Element-25-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">1u+14u+3×16u=63u1u+14u+3×16u=63u" id="MathJax-Element-47-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">1u+14u+3×16u=63u1u+14u+3×16u=63u" id="MathJax-Element-26-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">1u+14u+3×16u=63u1u+14u+3×16u=63u" id="MathJax-Element-152-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">1u+14u+3×16u=63u1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1u+14u+3×16u=63u 1 \, \text{u} + 14 \, \text{u} + 3 \times 16 \, \text{u} = 63 \, \text{u} .
 
• This makes the molecular mass of HNO₃ equal to 63 u.
 
• Therefore, the correct option is 1, which corresponds to 63 u.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (u)**

 
 
• It is a standard unit of mass that quantifies mass on an atomic or molecular scale (atomic mass).
 
• One atomic mass unit is defined as one twelfth of the mass of a single carbon-12 atom.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Mass**
 
 
• The molecular mass of a substance is the mass of one molecule of that substance, measured in atomic mass units (u).
 
• It is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of Molecular Mass**
 
 
• To calculate the molecular mass, identify the number of atoms of each element in the molecule.
 
• Multiply the atomic mass of each element by the number of atoms of that element.
 
• Add the results to obtain the molecular mass.

questions.question: ________ came to the conclusion that in every chemical reaction, total masses of all the reactants is equal to the masses of all the products. This law is known as the law of conservation of mass.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

Law of conservation of mass: ​Antoine Laurent Lavoisier gave this law. 

__
 
• According to the law of conservation of mass, The matter can be neither created nor destroyed.
 
• In other words, the mass of an object or collection of objects never changes, no matter how the parts are rearranged.
 
• In an ordinary chemical reaction, the sum of the masses of the reactants (the substances undergoing the change) equals the sum of the masses of the products (the substances formed during the process).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28fa049d4122d4bc120b00b7957ca5834ed8534c8717d2b9ad90865d83ba8c94.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Law of multiple proportions: Law of multiple proportions states that if two elements can combine to form more than one compound with each other, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in ratios of small whole numbers. 

Compounds of differing mass ratios of the same elements are found, but they will have different properties. 

Example: CO2 and CO

Law of definite proportion: Regardless of the amount, a compound is always composed of the same elements in the same proportion by mass. 

The proportions are found by calculating the percent by mass.

questions.question: Which of the following molecules doesn't include an ion bond in its formation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H2O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **H2O**, commonly known as water, consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
 
• The bonds in H2O are **covalent bonds**, where atoms share electrons to achieve a full outer shell.
 
• Each hydrogen atom shares one electron with the oxygen atom, resulting in two covalent bonds.
 
• Unlike ionic bonds, which involve the transfer of electrons, covalent bonds involve the sharing of electrons between atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ionic Bonds**

 
 
• Ionic bonds are formed when one atom transfers electrons to another atom, leading to the formation of ions.
 
• Common in compounds formed between metals and non-metals, such as NaCl (table salt).
 
• In ionic bonds, the resulting ions are held together by electrostatic forces.
 
 
 
• **Covalent Bonds**
 
 
• Covalent bonds involve the sharing of electron pairs between atoms.
 
• Common in organic molecules and many non-metal compounds, such as CO2 (carbon dioxide).
 
• Covalent bonds can be single, double, or triple, depending on the number of shared electron pairs.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Molecules with Ionic Bonds**
 
 
• LiCl (Lithium Chloride): Formed by the transfer of an electron from lithium to chlorine.
 
• MgO (Magnesium Oxide): Formed by the transfer of two electrons from magnesium to oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Molecules with Covalent Bonds**
 
 
• CH4 (Methane): Formed by the sharing of electrons between one carbon and four hydrogen atoms.
 
• O2 (Oxygen): Consists of two oxygen atoms sharing two pairs of electrons (double bond).

questions.question: The Law of Constant Proportions states that:

options.text: the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in a chemical reaction
energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed
the pressure of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature at constant volume
a given chemical compound always contains its component elements in a fixed ratio by mass

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**a given chemical compound always contains its component elements in a fixed ratio by mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Constant Proportions**, also known as the Law of Definite Proportions, is a fundamental principle in **chemistry**.
 
• It states that a given **chemical compound** always contains its **constituent elements** in the same proportion by **mass**, regardless of the source or method of preparation.
 
• This law was first formulated by **Joseph Proust** in 1797 and is a key part of the foundational principles of **stoichiometry**.
 
• For example, water (**H₂O**) always consists of **2 parts hydrogen** and **16 parts oxygen** by mass, irrespective of its source (river, sea, or laboratory).
 
• The law forms the basis for understanding the concept of **fixed ratios** in chemical reactions and compounds, which is crucial for accurate chemical formulations.
 
• It also supports the idea that compounds are composed of **atoms**, which combine in fixed ratios to form molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in a chemical reaction**__

 __
 
• This statement refers to the **Law of Conservation of Mass**.
 
• The law was established by **Antoine Lavoisier** in the late 18th century.
 
• It states that **mass cannot be created or destroyed** in a chemical reaction, but it can change form.
 
• This principle is widely used in **chemical equations** to balance reactions.
 
 
 
• **Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed**__
 __
 
• This describes the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, which is a principle of **physics**, not chemistry.
 
• It explains that **energy** in a closed system remains constant and can only be transferred or converted from one form to another (e.g., kinetic to potential energy).
 
 
 
• **The pressure of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature at constant volume**__
 
 
• This is a description of **Gay-Lussac's Law**, a gas law in **thermodynamics**.
 
• It states that at a constant volume, the **pressure** of an ideal gas is proportional to its **absolute temperature**.
 
• This law is part of the combined gas laws used to understand the behavior of gases under different conditions.

questions.question: A compound contains 4% hydrogen, 24% carbon and 71% chlorine. Its molar mass is 99 g. Its molecular formula is:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **The molecular formula **is the formula of a compound that shows its **constituent atoms** and **their number** per molecule denoted by **subscripts**.
 
• Molecular formula if known can be used to calculate:
 
 
• **Molecular mass **or** molar mass.**
 
• **Percentage of elements **in the compound**.**
 
 
 
• **​**If the** percentage composition **and** molar mass **is known, then it can be used to calculate the** empirical formula **which represents the formula in the simplest whole-number ratio.
 
• The **empirical formula **gives us the **Molecular formula** as:

Molecular formula = {( {Empirical formula} )_n} where n = largest ratio.

**Calculation:__**

**Given:**

 
• The compound contains:
 
 
• 4% hydrogen
 
• 24% carbon
 
• 71% chlorine
 
 
 
• **The molar mass** of the compound = **99 g**.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Elements
 Atomic mass
 % composition
 Atomic ratio
 **Simplest ratio**
 
 

 H
 1
 4
 {4 over 1} =4
 {4 over 2} =2
 
 

 C
 12
 24
 {24 over 12} =2
 {2 over 2} =1
 
 

 Cl
 35.5
 71
 {71 over 35.5} =2
 {2 over 2} =1
 
 

 
• The** empirical formula **comes as ** CH₂Cl**.
 
• We know,

Molecular formula = {( {Empirical formula} )_n}

 
• The molecular formula is given by (CH2Cl)₂ which becomes **C2H4Cl2**.

Hence, the compound which contains 4% hydrogen, 24% carbon, and 71% chlorine, and a molar mass is 99g is C2H4Cl2.

questions.question: A student calculates the formula unit mass of calcium fluoride (CaF₂). If the atomic masses of Ca and F are 40 u and 19 u, respectively, what is the correct formula unit mass?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**78 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formula unit mass of **Calcium Fluoride (CaF2)** is calculated by summing up the atomic masses of its constituent atoms.
 
• The atomic mass of **Calcium (Ca)** is given as **40 u**, and the atomic mass of **Fluorine (F)** is **19 u**.
 
• In the formula for Calcium Fluoride (CaF2), there is **1 atom of Calcium (Ca)** and **2 atoms of Fluorine (F)**.
 
• To calculate the formula unit mass:
 
 
• Mass contribution from Calcium = **1 × 40 u = 40 u**.
 
• Mass contribution from Fluorine = **2 × 19 u = 38 u**.
 
• Total formula unit mass = **40 u + 38 u = 78 u**.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct formula unit mass of Calcium Fluoride is **78 u**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formula Unit Mass:**

 
 
• The formula unit mass refers to the **sum of the atomic masses** of all atoms in a chemical formula of a compound.
 
• It is expressed in **atomic mass units (u)**.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Fluoride (CaF2):**
 
 
• **Calcium Fluoride** is an ionic compound consisting of **Calcium (Ca²⁺)** cations and **Fluoride (F⁻)** anions.
 
• It is widely used in industries, especially in **optics**, as it has excellent transparency to ultraviolet and infrared light.

questions.question: The atomic mass of an element is usually expressed in which of the following units?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic mass units (amu)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atomic mass units (amu) are the standard unit of mass that quantifies the mass of an atom or molecule.
 
• 1 amu is defined as one twelfth (1/12) of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
 
• The atomic mass unit allows chemists to compare the masses of different atoms on a scale that is easy to use and understand.
 
• The unit is widely used in chemistry and physics to express atomic and molecular weights.
 
• Atomic mass units are essential for understanding chemical reactions, molecular structures, and isotopic compositions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes:**

 
 
• Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons and thus different atomic masses.
 
• Examples include Carbon-12, Carbon-13, and Carbon-14.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass:**
 
 
• The mass of one mole of a substance (usually expressed in g/mol).
 
• It is numerically equal to the atomic or molecular mass in amu but expressed in grams.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Number:**
 
 
• The number of atoms, ions, or molecules in one mole of a substance, approximately 6.022 x 10²³.
 
• This constant is used to convert between atomic mass units and grams.
 
 
 
• **Relative Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• A weighted average of the atomic masses of an element's isotopes.
 
• It reflects the abundance of each isotope in nature.

questions.question: What does the subscript in a chemical formula represent?

options.text: The oxidation state of the element
The number of atoms of each element in a molecule

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The number of atoms of each element in a molecule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Subscripts in Chemical Formulas:**

 
• A subscript in a chemical formula is a number written below and to the right of an element's symbol.
 
• It indicates the number of atoms of that specific element present in a molecule or formula unit of the compound.
 
• For example, in the formula H₂O, the subscript "2" indicates that there are two hydrogen atoms.
 
• The absence of a subscript implies that there is only one atom of that element.
 
• Subscripts are used to accurately represent the composition of chemical compounds.
 
• They are essential for writing balanced chemical equations.
 
• Subscripts are integral to understanding the stoichiometry of chemical reactions.
 
• They provide crucial information about the molecular structure of compounds.
 
• Subscripts are used in ionic compounds to show the ratio of ions in the formula unit.
 
• They are also used in covalent compounds to show the actual number of atoms in a molecule.
 
• Subscripts are a fundamental part of chemical notation.
 
• They allow scientists to communicate the exact composition of substances.
 
• The subscript is always a whole number.
 
• Subscripts are used in empirical and molecular formulas.
 
• They help to distinguish between different compounds with similar elements.
 
• Subscripts provide the quantitative information about elements in a compound.
 
• They are vital for calculating molar masses and performing other stoichiometric calculations.
 
• Subscripts are used to denote the number of atoms present in a polyatomic ion, when that ion is included multiple times in a compound.
 
• Subscripts are used to show the ratio of elements in a compound.
 
• Subscripts are a vital part of chemical shorthand.

questions.question: Which pair of compounds illustrates the Law of Multiple Proportions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CO and CO₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Law of Multiple Proportions **states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a simple whole-number ratio.
 
• Carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) are compounds of carbon and oxygen that follow this law.
 
• In CO, the ratio of carbon to oxygen by mass is 12:16, while in CO₂, it is 12:32. The oxygen mass ratio between CO and CO₂ is 16:32, which simplifies to 1:2.
 
• This simple whole-number ratio (1:2) illustrates the Law of Multiple Proportions.
 
• The law was proposed by John Dalton in 1804 and is one of the basic principles of stoichiometry in chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions:**

 
 
• It is one of the fundamental laws of chemical combination in chemistry.
 
• This law applies when two elements form more than one compound, such as CO and CO₂, or SO₂ and SO₃.
 
• The law emphasizes the discrete nature of chemical combinations, underscoring the concept of fixed proportions in compounds.
 
 
 
• **Examples of the Law:**
 
 
• Water (H₂O) and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) — The ratio of oxygen masses is 1:2.
 
• Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and sulfur trioxide (SO₃) — The ratio of oxygen masses is 2:3.
 
 
 
• **John Dalton:**
 
 
• He is known as the "Father of Modern Chemistry" for his Atomic Theory, which includes the Law of Multiple Proportions.
 
• His work laid the foundation for modern stoichiometry and molecular chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry:**
 
 
• It is the quantitative study of reactants and products in a chemical reaction.
 
• The Law of Multiple Proportions is a cornerstone of stoichiometric calculations.

questions.question: How much oxygen can be obtained from 90 Kg of water?
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

Law of constant proportions:

__
 
• Many scientists, noted that many compounds when made up of two or more elements contained the elements in the same proportions irrespective of the mode of their preparation.
 
• Such as, the ratio of the mass of hydrogen to that of **oxygen** is always 1:8, whatever may be the source of water.
 
• It indicates, that if 9g of water is decomposed, 1g of hydrogen and 8g of oxygen will be liberated.
 
• This led to the law of constant proportions which states that ' In a chemical substance, the elements are always present in definite proportions by mass '.
 
• This law was formulated by Lavoisier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38f9e70433e3384e22d6f653af2cd27190bcdfdf184912ab85941f0eb43c1871.png] 

Law of conservation of mass:

 
• Mass in an isolated system can neither be created nor destroyed.
 
• During a chemical process, the mass of the elements is the same as before after the reaction.

**Calculation:**__

__
 
• The decomposition of water occurs as follows:

**H₂O → H₂ + O₂**

 
• In water, the ratio of the mass of hydrogen to that of **oxygen** is 1:8.
 
• So, when water decomposes, it produces hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio of 1:8.
 
• So, when 90 kg of water decomposes, 10 kg of hydrogen and 80kg of oxygen is produced.
 
• The total mass before and after the decomposition is 90kg.

Hence, 80 kg of **oxygen** can be obtained **from 90 Kg of water.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

Law of multiple proportions:

 
• When two or more compounds are formed by the combination of two elements, the weight of one element that combines with the other is in simple ratios of whole numbers.
 
• When oxides of nitrogen are formed with oxygen, the masses of oxygen are 8g,16g, 24g, 32g etc. the ratio is 1:2:3:4.
 
• It was formulated by Dalton.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct unit mass of sodium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The atomic mass of sodium (Na) is **23 unified atomic mass units (u)**.
 
• Sodium is represented by the symbol **Na** on the periodic table.
 
• Sodium's atomic number is **11**, indicating it has 11 protons.
 
• The atomic mass is calculated primarily from the number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unified Atomic Mass Unit (u)**

 
 
• It is a standard unit of mass that quantifies mass on an atomic or molecular scale.
 
• 1 unified atomic mass unit is defined as one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table**
 
 
• It is a tabular display of the chemical elements, organized on the basis of their atomic numbers, electron configurations, and recurring chemical properties.
 
• Elements are presented in order of increasing atomic number.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes**
 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a particular chemical element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
 
• Sodium has several isotopes, but only sodium-23 is stable and naturally abundant.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties of Sodium**
 
 
• Sodium is a highly reactive metal and is part of the alkali metal group.
 
• It reacts vigorously with water to form sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.question: A group of more than three atoms carrying a charge is known as _________ ion.
questions.solution:
__**Polyatomic**__ is the correct answer.

__
 
• **Polyatomic__:**

 
 
• A group of** more than three atoms **carrying a charge is known as polyatomic ions. They carry a fixed charge on them.
 
• The atoms in a polyatomic ion are usually covalently bonded to one another and therefore stay together as a single, charged unit.
 
• Example: Ammonium NH₄⁺, Nitrate NO³⁻, Carbonate CO₃²–
 
 
 
• **Tri atomic**
 
 
• Tri atomic are those molecules that contain** three atoms **of the same or different chemical elements**.**
 
• Example: H₂O, CO₂
 
 
 
• **Monoatomic​:**
 
 
• **Monoatomic **are molecules** only with one atom **and lack a covalent bond.
 
• Example: all noble gases are an example of it as helium (He), neon (Ne), argon (Ar), krypton (Kr).
 
 
 
• **Di atomic:**
 
 
• A molecule of** two-atom **either of the same element or different elements.
 
• Example: O₂, H₂

questions.question: Calculate the molecular mass of ammonia, NH₃, using the provided atomic masses (Atomic mass of N = 14 u and H= 1 u).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **molecular mass** of a compound is calculated by adding the **atomic masses** of all the constituent atoms in the molecule.
 
• In ammonia (**NH₃**), there is **1 nitrogen atom** and **3 hydrogen atoms**.
 
• The **atomic mass of nitrogen** is given as **14 u**.
 
• The **atomic mass of hydrogen** is given as **1 u**.
 
• To calculate the molecular mass of ammonia:
 
 
• Molecular mass = Atomic mass of nitrogen + (Atomic mass of hydrogen × Number of hydrogen atoms).
 
• Molecular mass = **14 u** + (**1 u** × **3**).
 
• Molecular mass = **14 u** + **3 u**.
 
• Molecular mass = **17 u**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the molecular mass of ammonia is **17 u**.
 
• This value is crucial in **chemical calculations** such as determining molar masses or balancing equations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Mass**__

 
 
• The **atomic mass** of an element is the weighted average mass of all the isotopes of that element.
 
• It is expressed in **atomic mass units (u)**, where 1 u is defined as one-twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
 
• Atomic mass is a crucial concept in **chemistry** for calculating molecular masses and performing stoichiometric calculations.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about molecules of elements is correct?

options.text: Molecular oxygen and ozone are both molecules of the same element.
Diatomic molecules only contain atoms of different elements.
All elements exist as monoatomic molecules in nature.
A molecule of phosphorus always contains five atoms.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is:** "Molecular oxygen and ozone are both molecules of the same element."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Definition of Elemental Molecules:**

 
 
• An elemental molecule is made up of atoms of the same chemical element bonded together.
 
• For example, oxygen exists in nature as O₂ (molecular oxygen) and O₃ (ozone), both containing only oxygen atoms.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Oxygen (O₂): **
 
 
• It is a diatomic molecule comprising two oxygen atoms bonded together.
 
• Molecular oxygen is essential for respiration in most living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Ozone (O₃): **
 
 
• It is a triatomic molecule made up of three oxygen atoms bonded together.
 
• Ozone plays a crucial role in absorbing harmful ultraviolet radiation in the Earth's stratosphere.
 
 
 
• **Commonality:**
 
 
• Both O₂ and O₃ are allotropes of the element oxygen, differing in molecular composition but made of the same element.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Diatomic molecules only contain atoms of different elements."**

 
 
• **Incorrect Explanation:** Diatomic molecules can be either homonuclear (same element, e.g., O₂, N₂, H₂) or heteronuclear (different elements, e.g., HCl, CO).
 
• **Correct Concept:** Diatomic refers to the number of atoms, not the type of atoms involved.
 
 
 
• **"All elements exist as monoatomic molecules in nature."**
 
 
• **Incorrect Explanation:** While noble gases like helium (He), neon (Ne), and argon (Ar) exist as monoatomic gases, many other elements exist as diatomic or polyatomic molecules (e.g., O₂, N₂, S₈).
 
• **Correct Concept:** The physical form of an element depends on its chemical bonding and stability in nature.
 
 
 
• **"A molecule of phosphorus always contains five atoms."**
 
 
• **Incorrect Explanation:** Phosphorus typically exists as P₄ molecules, meaning it contains four phosphorus atoms in a tetrahedral arrangement.
 
• **Correct Concept:** There is no common form of phosphorus containing five atoms in a single molecule.
